LESSON: READING 10.2.1 FLUENCY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Festivals Suggested vocabulary wedding, birthday, Christmas, Easter, Idd, Diwali
Topic 10.2: Reading 10.2.1 Fluency
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 10.2.1 Fluency, part of Festivals Suggested vocabulary wedding, birthday, Christmas, Easter, Idd, Diwali in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: when reading. How can we improve our reading speed?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 10.2.1 Fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn: The learner’s ability to learn independently is enhanced as they practise reading texts at the right speed and with the right

expressions on their own.

Values:
Respect is cultivated as the learner appreciates the effort of peers during timed reading and gives positive feedback.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (Self-esteem): The learner’s self-esteem is raised as they acquire reading fluency skills.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner applies reading fluency skills acquired in learning of texts in Kiswahili Language Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

• Print textbooks in appropriate font size and colour contrast

• Braille books

• Digital devices with assistive technology,

• Charts, flash cards or braille cards,

• Pictures or picture description
